scope.summary: The library changes add a gzprintf/gzvprintf stub, an --insecure configure option, ZLIB_INSECURE guards, a new zlibCompileFlags bit and documentation updates. None of them breaks the old harness: it reaches gzprintf and zlibCompileFlags, and it ignores their return values. However, the harness has a preexisting defect in the seek case (case 4). It indexes a 5-element whences array with (byte % 6), so index 5 is an out-of-bounds stack read. A 3-byte input triggers it, and it makes the target's execution invalid (J2).

assessments.reason: FAQ prose only. It is not compiled and has no effect on the build or on gzprintf calls.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The build uses configure and make; the FAQ is not used.

assessments.reason: insecure now defaults to 0. build.sh runs ./configure with no options, so this is the default secure build, and behavior that only --insecure enables is out of scope (D6).
Adds the --insecure option, which the build recipe never passes.
-DZLIB_INSECURE is added only when insecure=1, which never happens under the supplied recipe.
Adds warning echoes only; there is no exit or change to the build.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: configure failure is checked, but echoes do not cause failure.

assessments.reason: The guard keeps gz_vacate whenever the printf path is compiled. The harness's gzprintf calls reach gzvprintf, which calls gz_vacate.
gzprintf calls gzvprintf, and the harness reaches it. Whether the stub or the real body is compiled, the harness ignores the return value, so execution stays valid.
Closes the stub #if in gzvprintf. Reached through the same gzprintf route.
Stub for the old-style gzprintf variant. If that variant is compiled, the harness gzprintf calls reach it, and their results are ignored.
Changes the error field name (error to err) in the old-style variant. It is reached by the same gzprintf calls, and their results are unchecked.
Closes the stub #if in the old-style variant. Reached by the same route.
Documentation comment describing the zlibCompileFlags bits.
The STDC/stdarg guard selects the variadic prototype, which the harness gzprintf calls use.
zlibCompileFlags is called in case 23 and its result is ignored. The changed flag bits cannot break any harness check.

build.reason: build.sh runs a default configure, builds libz.a, then compiles each *_fuzzer.c against it. All APIs the harness uses are declared in zlib.h.

input.reason: In case 4, whences has 5 elements but is indexed with (*data)%6, so index 5 reads out of bounds. Input bytes 00 04 05 reach it.

lifecycle.reason: Case 21 calls gzclose_r and then sets file to NULL, even if the handle is in write mode. Whether gzclose_r frees a write handle is not supplied.

evidence.dependency_reason: gzclose handles NULL; gzclose_r body not supplied.

control_flow.reason: The op loop dispatches on byte%26 to every case. Each API used checks for a NULL file, so the loop works even when gzopen fails.

missing_information: gzclose_r body (gzclose.c / gzread.c) for the lifecycle of write handles

blockers.requirement: The harness's seek operation must choose whence from a valid index into its own whences array.
blockers.failure_condition: Input 00 04 05: mode_sz=2, so the copy into mode does not advance data. The op byte 0x04 selects case 4, and the next byte gives 0x05%6 = 5, which reads whences[5] of a 5-element stack array. That is an out-of-bounds read (undefined behavior; ASan reports it).
blockers.alternative_paths: None. The harness's own decoding performs the read before gzseek is called, so no input avoids it once that byte value is chosen.

assumptions: Default ./configure in build.sh defines neither ZLIB_INSECURE nor anything that changes the harness's gzprintf route.
